editorial.headline: Money-Market and FX Support: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This intermediary market activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership, yet a permanent Bali PMA moratorium blocks registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
**For a foreign-owned company, this activity cannot be registered at a Bali address today.** Nationally, the activity is open to PMA and permits foreign ownership of up to 100%. Bali reaches a different result. Its island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium blocks every Low and Medium-Low risk activity for a Bali address. The Large-scale entry for this activity is classified as Medium-Low, bringing it inside that block. The restriction concerns PMA registration, not a recalculation of the national foreign-ownership ceiling. Bali’s address-based rule controls even though the national status remains open.

The underlying work is intermediary activity in the money and foreign-exchange markets. It encompasses intermediation connected with the issue and trading of instruments, together with execution of transactions in those markets, provided the activity is conducted other than through an exchange. Money-market and foreign-exchange markets are both named in the scope, as are both instrument-related work and transaction-related work. The scope brings the intermediary side of issuance and trading together with transaction execution. The exclusion of exchange-based execution marks the boundary set by the recorded scope.

Businesses undertaking that intermediary work may register it at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah or Besar scale under the national framework. The record expressly includes the activity across those four categories; it does not confine the stated scope to one business size. For a PMA applicant, however, scale is more than a descriptive label when the registered address is in Bali. The Bali record points to the Besar-scale classification in explaining why PMA registration is blocked. National scale coverage does not displace that Bali-specific rule.

That makes the national-versus-Bali picture clear. The national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, supported in the record by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali’s rule is a full PMA registration block for the Bali address. It is tied to Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, dated May 13, 2026, and is described as permanent. A founder can read the code as nationally open without mistaking that status for present PMA availability in Bali: for this activity, a Bali address remains blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a PMA registration route at a Bali address for this activity.
